channel.title: GovConCEO Executive Intelligence Brief
channel.description: Reports for U.S. government contractors, sourced to official primary documents. Not legal advice.

item.title: USTR Extends All 178 Current Section 301 China Product Exclusions
item.description: A Nov 10 Federal Register notice further extends all 178 current Section 301 exclusions on certain products of China. The annexes cover goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time November 10, 2026, and before 11:59 p.m. eastern time January 9, 2027. The determination paragraph also says the exclusions are extended until January 10, 2027.

item.title: DoD Removes WuXi AppTec From the Section 1260H List, Without Prejudice to Relisting
item.description: A Nov 10 Department of Defense notice removes WuXi AppTec Co., Ltd. from the Section 1260H list published June 10, 2026, in compliance with a preliminary injunction, without prejudice to relisting on additional or supplementary grounds. The opened official texts describe listing and delisting duties, not a general clearance to do business.

item.title: HUD Will Reorganize Its Operating Model, Including a Centralized Early-Acquisition Hub at OCPO
item.description: A Nov 10 HUD notice of intent does not propose any office closures or relocation of staff. The Office of the Chief Procurement Officer will establish a centralized hub for early acquisition life-cycle activities. HUD will begin the reorganization approximately 90 days after November 10, 2026.

item.title: USTR Extends the Vietnam Section 301 Investigation; Determinations Due by February 28, 2027
item.description: A USTR notice published Nov 10, 2026, and effective Nov 3, 2026, extends the Vietnam intellectual-property Section 301 investigation by three months. Determinations will be made by no later than February 28, 2027. The notice does not impose duties or publish an exclusion list.

item.title: Reading Agency Procurement Forecasts: What They Promise, What They Don't, and How Agencies Publish Them
item.description: A narrowed, source-checked guide to federal procurement forecasts: the legal basis agencies cite, what GSA's governmentwide Forecast of Contracting Opportunities tool contains and disclaims, and how four agencies actually publish and update their forecasts.

item.title: How Continuing Resolutions Work: New Starts, Funding Rates and What They Do to Awards
item.description: The mechanics of the FY2027 continuing resolution (P.L. 119-103), clause by clause: the funding rate, the new-start ban, the DoD production limits, the "most limited funding action" rule, anomalies, and the FAR tools contracting officers use during a CR.

item.title: FY2027 Is Running on a Continuing Resolution Through December 11
item.description: Nov 10, 2026: FY2027 is running on a continuing resolution (P.L. 119-103) through December 11. No regular appropriations act was located. The House passed the FY2027 NDAA 216–212 on July 22.

item.title: RFO Part-by-Part Tracker: 53 FAR Parts, 8 Proposed Rules, 15 Parts Still Waiting
item.description: Where every FAR part stands in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul as of Nov 7, 2026: model deviation date, latest update, proposed rule, and comment deadline.

item.title: SSP and POA&M: What Assessors Look For, Per NIST 800-171A and the CMMC Rule
item.description: The assessment objectives for the system security plan (3.12.4) and plans of action (3.12.2), the CMMC POA&M limits in 32 CFR 170.21, and what DOJ settlements say about missing plans.

item.title: SPRS Scores Explained: What the 110-Point Number Means at Award, and Who Checks It
item.description: How DFARS 252.204-7019, 252.204-7020 and 204.7303 use the SPRS summary score, what counts as current, and how the 110-point scale works.

item.title: Cyber Compliance Is False Claims Act Risk: 18 DOJ Cyber-Fraud Resolutions Since 2022, Totaling About $82.5 Million
item.description: Every DOJ cybersecurity False Claims Act resolution found in DOJ's official press-release records since the Civil Cyber-Fraud Initiative launched in October 2021, with amounts, theories and whistleblower shares.

item.title: Vetting Sub-Tier Suppliers: A Prime Contractor’s Checklist Built From the Clauses That Already Apply
item.description: The prime owns subcontractor responsibility. FAR 9.104-4 says prospective primes are generally responsible for determining the responsibility of their prospective subcontractors. A weak subcontractor can affect the Government’s view of the prime. Exclusions check above $45,000. FAR 52.

item.title: Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Enters Formal Rulemaking, With No Final Rules Yet
item.description: Nov 1, 2026: Eight of twelve Revolutionary FAR Overhaul proposed rules have been published. Comment periods have closed. No final rules were located. Part 19 has not been proposed.

item.title: Defense Supply-Chain Waivers Tighten on January 1, as FASCSA Orders Hit DeepSeek and Acronis
item.description: Oct 31, 2026: EO 14415 tightens 10 U.S.C. 4872 waivers as of January 1, 2027, and directs all-tier mapping policy by January 16, 2027. DHS FASCSA orders cover DeepSeek and Acronis products.

item.title: FASCSA Exclusion Orders Explained: Two Are Now Public, and Contractors Must Check SAM Every Three Months
item.description: Two orders are public. DHS Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01 covers DeepSeek (released July 24, 2026). Order #2026-02 covers Acronis (released July 31, 2026). Their Federal Register notices appeared October 20 and October 30, 2026. They reach contractors.

item.title: Post-Quantum Deadlines Are Set: 2030 for Key Exchange, 2031 for Signatures, and a FAR Rule Due by December 19
item.description: A contractor rule is coming. Executive Order 14412 directs the FAR Council to propose, within 180 days of June 22, 2026 (by December 19, 2026), a rule requiring covered contractors to comply with NIST FIPS, including PQC standards, by December 31, 2030. ”Covered contractor” is not yet defined.

item.title: Defense vs. Civilian in the FY2027 Request: Defense Up 42.1%, Non-Defense Down 10.0%
item.description: Agency-by-agency comparison of the President's FY2027 discretionary request with FY2026 enacted levels, read straight from OMB's Table S-3. Requested numbers are proposals, not appropriations. Not financial advice.

item.title: Bid Protests Under the New FAR: What Changes at the Agency, What Stays at GAO and the Court of Federal Claims
item.description: FAR Case 2026-001 rewrites FAR Part 33 with a purpose statement, an incumbent-protest finding and more disclosure in agency protests, while GAO's statute and 4 CFR part 21 rules stay in place. Includes GAO's FY2025 protest statistics.

item.title: Cyber Clause Flow-Down Playbook: Which Clauses Go to Subcontractors, With What Exceptions
item.description: Clause-by-clause flow-down rules for DFARS 252.204-7012, -7020, -7021, 252.239-7010 and FAR 52.204-21, -23, -25, -27 and -30, and how the proposed FAR Part 40 would consolidate them.

item.title: No Federal Rule Bans AI-Written Bids. What the Official Record Says About Using AI on Proposals
item.description: The FAR is silent. The current FAR on Acquisition.gov (FAC 2026-01) does not use the term “artificial intelligence” in Parts 4, 9, 12, 15, 25, 27, 39, 44 or 52. The DFARS parts reviewed (225, 227, 252) do not use it either. No government-wide rule permits or prohibits AI-drafted proposals.

item.title: Year-End Spending: September Alone Was 19.5% of FY2025 Contract Obligations
item.description: Three fiscal years of USAspending contract obligations by month show a growing fourth-quarter surge. This report sets the data next to the rules that shape it: bona fide need, severable-service authority, the Antideficiency Act and DoD's 20 percent limit on the last two months. Narrowed to FY2023–FY2025. Not financial advice.

item.title: EO 14415’s Bill-of-Materials Mandate: What Defense Suppliers Must Map, and Which Dates Are Fixed So Far
item.description: Policy due January 16, 2027. EO 14415 gives the Secretary of War 180 days from July 20, 2026, to issue policy requiring primes and subcontractors at any tier to map critical supply chains from raw materials to end products. Implementing regulations follow within 90 days of the policy’s completion.

item.title: "Meaningful Negotiations" vs. "Discussions": What the FAR Part 15 Rewrite Changes in Competitive Range Exchanges
item.description: How FAR Case 2026-003 and the model Part 15 deviation replace "discussions" with "negotiation," redefine "deficiency," widen clarifications, and allow further negotiation with one offeror. Side-by-side with current FAR 15.306.

item.title: Commercial Buys Without 52.212-3 and 52.212-5: The Government Picks the Clauses, and Off-List Clauses Need a Deviation
item.description: FAR Case 2026-003 would remove the commercial omnibus provision and clause, shift clause selection to the Government, require a deviation for unlisted clauses, and fold simplified procedures up to $9 million into Part 12.

item.title: Who Owns the Data, the Model and the Outputs? How Federal Rules Split Rights in AI Contracts
item.description: Government data stays government. OMB tells agencies to retain rights to federal data and to improvements to it. GSA’s LLM clause states that the Government owns all Government Data, meaning both inputs and outputs, and all Custom Developments. Your model stays yours. Under GSAR 552.

item.title: GSA’s LLM Clause, Line by Line: What GSAR 552.239-7001 Requires and Why It Overrides Your Terms of Service
item.description: It beats your terms of service. The clause is incorporated into the “schedule of supplies/services,” the top of the commercial order of precedence. If it conflicts with a vendor’s terms of service, click-wrap or licence, the clause takes precedence. Narrow trigger, self-deleting.

item.title: CMMC Phase 2 Is Suspended: Only Level 1 and Level 2 Self-Assessments May Be Required
item.description: Oct 18, 2026: CMMC Phase 2 is suspended. Only Level 1 and Level 2 self-assessments may be required. NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 duties under DFARS 252.204-7012 remain in effect.

item.title: GSA’s LLM Clause Sets Data-Use Rules; OMB Rescinds a Software Attestation Mandate and Sets 2030 Cryptography Targets
item.description: Oct 17, 2026: GSA’s LLM clause sets data-use and diligence rules. OMB M-26-05 rescinds the governmentwide secure-software attestation mandate. EO 14412 directs a FAR proposed rule by December 19, 2026, with a December 31, 2030 contractor FIPS date.

item.title: DFARS 7012 Incident Reporting: The 72-Hour Clock, the 90-Day Hold, and Day-One Actions
item.description: What DFARS 252.204-7012 requires when a cyber incident hits covered defense information: review, report to DIBNet within 72 hours, submit malware to DC3, preserve images for 90 days, and pass the report number up the chain.

item.title: Small Business and FAR Part 19: Deviation in Force, No Proposed Rule Yet, and Three SBA Rules Moving
item.description: Where FAR Part 19 stands in the overhaul: the model deviation and GSA's supplement, the rule of two, order set-asides "not a basis for protest," and SBA's 8(a), program-wide and size-standard rulemakings. Size-standard comments are due Nov 20, 2026.

item.title: Three OMB Memos Set the Terms for Selling AI to Civilian Agencies. Here Is What Vendors Must Deliver
item.description: Three memos govern. OMB M-25-21 (use and risk management) and M-25-22 (acquisition), both dated April 3, 2025, and M-26-04 (Unbiased AI Principles for LLMs), dated December 11, 2025, set the federal civilian baseline for AI contracts. All three are listed on OMB’s memoranda page as of October 14, 2026.

item.title: Agency Reorganizations and Your Contracts: Five Executive Orders in Force, a Budget Full of Proposals
item.description: What has actually been ordered (EOs 14222, 14240, 14242, 14372, 14402) versus what the FY2027 Budget only proposes (USDA hubs, the U.S. Wildland Fire Service, HHS's Administration for a Healthy America, DHS consolidation, OCTAE to Labor), and what each means for contract scope, buying offices and pricing.

item.title: Section 889 Due Diligence: The Representation, the One-Business-Day Report and What the FAR Overhaul Would Change
item.description: Two prohibitions, both in force. Since August 13, 2019, contractors may not provide covered telecom to the Government. Since August 13, 2020, agencies may not contract with an entity that uses covered telecom as a substantial or essential component of any system, whether or not the use is on federal work.

item.title: Buy American Content Rises to 75% in 2029, and the 55% Fallback Ends in 2030: The Schedule to Price In Now
item.description: 65% now, 75% from 2029. Under FAR 25.101, a manufactured end product is domestic only if its domestic components cost more than 65% of all components for items delivered in 2024 through 2028. The figure rises to 75% for items delivered from calendar year 2029. Delivery year controls.
